title: Studentized Inference for Adaptive Experiments with Random Limiting Quadratic Variation
banked_reason: Cold referee: the field lift needs separate switching-layer, compact-uniform hitting/escape, and Gaussian-to-bounded bridge theory; the current conditional result is sound at subfield tier.
gap_reasons: The finite-attractor mixed-normal and pivotality results assume finite tail selection and a vanishing uniform Cesaro-attraction modulus; these load-bearing dynamics are not established for the Guo--Xu recursion, and the HeartSteps discussion is only a consumer interpretation.

The deterministic-sandwich iff statements are conditional scale-mixture identification and polarization results, leaving the unverified recursion-to-class bridge as the specific obstacle to field tier.

It does not characterize validity on Saco's published variance-growth class, so the framing of an inference frontier or exact temporal boundary overstates a sufficient condition plus one violating witness.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery discharged all 19 obligations (14 proved and five source-attested cited interfaces), including the bounded Saco counterexample, early-stabilization repair, conditional finite-attractor mixture/pivot results, sandwich characterizations, and the four-mode Guo--Xu obstruction. Formalization reached F2.5 and forced several source-faithfulness repairs, but the final cold novelty review found that field tier still requires a separate proof of Guo--Xu switching-layer escape, compact-uniform attraction, and a bridge from the published Gaussian recursion to the bounded causal-score setting. The current conditional result is sound at subfield tier; it was banked for a future re-raised run rather than weakening the field floor.
tldr: The field-tier contribution is a conditional finite-attractor theorem bundle for adaptive causal IPW-Z inference. Under common score, derivative, Jacobian-lower-bound, policy, covariance-lower-bound, root-separation, attraction, and local root-search envelopes, with attainable basins defined as the positive-mass support of the tail selector and with \(r_T+\delta_T\to0\), the bundle derives a basin-stable finite Gaussian mixture with predictable-QV error controlled by \(r_T+\delta_T\), proves that an always-defined same-path realized-QV sandwich is uniformly pivotal and asymptotically untruncated, and gives exact deterministic-sandwich boundaries: every-level validity for one contrast holds if and only if that contrast's variance is basin-invariant, while validity for all contrasts holds if and only if the full covariance is deterministic. The separate early-stabilized projected class uses only the scaled numerical-tolerance condition \(T^{-1/2}(r_T+\delta_T)\to0\). Theorem 2 has one direct strict-tightening comparator, Saco's pointwise realized-QV result; the remaining named papers provide motivation, ingredients, or orthogonal regimes rather than a second strict frontier. An elementary bounded two-basin law verifies that contrastwise invariance need not imply matrix invariance. The slope-projected limit set of the augmented bounded Guo--Xu Markov chain remains an open dynamics question with no class-membership or inference claim.
gap: Saco supplies the one direct pointwise realized-QV comparator, but not uniform verification over an endogenous finite-attractor class. Guo--Xu and Shen and coauthors supply adjacent stable-policy and directional-stability results, Han studies continuous SDE-invariant Thompson-sampling pull proportions and raw-arm-mean inference, and Leiner, Dunn, and Ramdas study stationary-evaluation-policy off-policy M-estimation with flexible variance stabilization under unstable logging. Zhang, Janson, and Murphy instead study pooled longitudinal adaptive sampling with Z-estimation and an adaptive sandwich estimator in a fixed-within-user, growing-participant regime. Existing stochastic-approximation results control lock-in only after entry into an attraction domain, and the Guo--Xu two-mode example remains numerical.
fill: The publishable contribution is the conditional finite-attractor theorem bundle: a basin-stable causal IPW-Z finite Gaussian mixture, a uniformly feasible same-path realized-QV pivot, and exact contrastwise and matrixwise deterministic-sandwich boundaries. A finite-attractor class indexed by common score, derivative, Jacobian lower, policy, covariance lower, root-separation, attraction, and local root-search envelopes converts policy dynamics into predictable-QV control with error \(r_T+\delta_T\); its attainable-basin index set is the positive-mass support of the tail selector. The score and derivative envelopes already imply \(\Omega_j\preceq(KB^2/\varepsilon)I_d\) and \(\|H\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le KD_1\), so no primitive upper matrix bounds are imposed. The proposal-specific envelope \(e_T=T^{-1/2}+r_T+\delta_T\) combines sampling, attraction, and approximation errors. A preliminary moment-norm minimizer localizes a compact empirical-root set; martingale concentration and a quantitative inverse-function argument make the exact-root selector active with probability tending uniformly to one. Stable martingale convergence supplies the mixture, event-truncated realized QV supplies the feasible pivot, finite normal-mixture identification plus polarization supplies the two necessity results, and a bounded in-class law certifies strict logical separation of the directional and matrix frontiers.
